newsitem.title: USA: Exabyte Q4 hurt by soft demand, writedowns.
newsitem.headline: Exabyte Q4 hurt by soft demand, writedowns.

text.p: Exabyte Corp said its fouth quarter was hurt by soft demand and inventory writedowns and supply constraints.
The company said its decision to discontinue the 4mm DAT product line early in 1996 resulted in a $20 million revenue reduction but a better bottom line for the year.

Overall demand was softer than expected, and several million dollars of orders went unfulfilled due to the supply constraints mentioned previously. Operating expenses during the quarter were unusually high, the company said, in part due to a payment to a development partner.

It also had higher than usual prototype and engineering development costs for new products and recorded a bad debt charge during the quarter. Start-up costs were also incurred for new service depots in Singapore, Canada and Australia.

The company said it has begun to ship several significant products in 1996 -- Mammoth, Eagle Travan- 3 and Travan-4, the Eagle Nest, and the EXB-220 library -- and hope to introduce several more in 1997.

Earlier, the company reported revenue for the year ended December 28, 1996, of $362,890,000 versus revenue of $374,147,000 for the prior year. Net income increased to $8,625,000 or $0.39 per share in 1996 from a loss of $12,435,000 or $0.57 per share in 1995. The 1995 loss reflected substantial inventory write-downs, goodwill write-offs and reserves which were established during the third quarter of that year. Without such adjustments, the net income for 1995 was $10,116,000 or $0.47 per share.

Revenue for the fourth quarter of 1996 was $85,868,000 versus $96,871,000 for the comparable period in the previous year. There was a net loss in the fourth quarter of 1996 of $2,043,000 or $0.09 per share versus net income in the prior year's fourth quarter of $3,267,000 or $0.15 per share.
